title: SSB-1 replacement traction battery for the Super Soco TS
audience_note: Written for investors and manufacturing partners who are deciding whether to fund or build SSB-1 beyond the prototype. It states what has been checked, what exists only on paper, what it would cost per unit at four volumes, and what each stage to mass production needs in time and money.

executive_summary.one_liner: A drop-in 60 V, 1.84 kWh replacement battery for a popular light electric motorcycle, designed down to every part, file and test, but not yet built.
paragraphs: SSB-1 is a removable 17S6P lithium-ion pack (61.2 V nominal, about 30 Ah, about 1.84 kWh) for the Super Soco TS, a 60 V light electric motorcycle. It pairs 102 Samsung 50S 21700 cells with a bought 17S smart BMS, a 60 A Class T fuse and a small custom gateway board that answers the bike's RS-485 battery polls, so the dash still shows charge and faults. The prototype housing is 3D printed PETG on four steel tie rods.

The design package is complete and machine-checked: parametric CAD, drawings in mm and inches, sliced G-code, a 6-gate bill-of-materials check, a KiCad board with 0 ERC and 0 DRC errors and a turnkey PCBA order package, and gateway firmware that builds and passes 120 host unit tests. Nothing has been built, flashed, fitted to a bike or ridden. Three facts that decide whether the pack fits a given bike (plug pin-out, lock geometry, bus protocol on a TS) are open and can be settled with under 100 USD of measurement.

The parts for one prototype cost about 1,866 USD at 2026-11-15 list prices; the comparable branded replacement lists at 1,250 EUR and was out of stock with a lead time of up to 12 weeks. Estimated cost of goods falls to about 860 USD at 100 units, about 510 USD at 1,000 and about 410 USD at 10,000, driven by cell price and by replacing the printed housing with flame-retardant moulded parts. Those volume figures are estimates; the cell figures rest on one distributor's published 600-piece price.

The largest gaps between this prototype and a product that can be sold are safety certification (UN 38.3 for transport, UL 2271 or EN 50604-1 for sale), a flame-retardant enclosure (proposal PROP-001), and tooling. Reaching a first 1,000-unit production run is estimated at 0.9 to 1.7 million USD over 18 to 30 months, most of it in certification test packs, tooling and inventory.

paragraphs: Light electric motorcycles and mopeds such as the Super Soco TS use a removable proprietary battery. When it wears out, owners depend on the brand's spare-part channel. The one comparable listing found during research was a 60 V 30 Ah pack at 1,250 EUR, out of stock, available to pre-order with a lead time of up to 12 weeks. A worn battery can therefore take a bike off the road for months and cost a large share of the bike's resale value.
SSB-1 aims to be a compatible pack built from standard, multi-sourced parts (cells, BMS, fuse, connectors) with a small interface board that keeps the bike's dash working.

evidence.claim: TS battery is 60 V, 26 Ah, 170 cells; controller current limit 40 A
A 60 V 30 Ah TC/TS replacement lists at 1,250 EUR incl. VAT, not in stock, pre-order with lead time under 12 weeks (read 2026-11-15)
Vmoto, the TS maker, reported revenue of about 46.8 million USD for FY2025

not_known: Installed base of TS, TC and TSX bikes by country, and how many are past their battery's service life. No unit-sales figure was found in public sources during this research. This is the first number an investor will ask for; get it from registration data (for example EU national registries) or a distributor.
Whether the same housing and gateway can serve the brand's other 60 V models (TC, TC Max, CPx) with a different cell layout or plug. That would decide whether this is one product or a family.
Willingness to pay for a non-original pack, and the role of warranty and insurance in that decision.

product.description: Removable pack, upright in the frame bay, locked by the bike's key lock, carried by a top handle, connected by one plug. 17 series groups of six cells in two welded bricks, held by printed cell holders between FR-4 barrier plates; BMS, fuse and gateway in the upper bay.

specs.value: Isolated RS-485, answers battery polls at address 0x5A

trl.why: Every subsystem is designed and checked by analysis and software tests; no hardware exists. TRL 4 needs the gateway board running on a bench and one cell brick built; TRL 6 needs a full pack running a bike.

mrl.why: Manufacturing concepts identified and a complete prototype build package exists. No production process, tooling or supplier has been qualified.

verified.item: Bill of materials complete and consistent
verified.how: 6-gate script check: every part BUY or BUILD, files on disk, assembly steps, CAD and schematic agree. PASS.
KiCad 10.0.8: 0 ERC errors, 0 DRC errors, 0 unconnected; Gerbers and turnkey PCBA package generated.
Builds for ESP32-C3; 120 of 120 host unit tests pass, including the whole gateway against simulated BMS and bike bus.
Meshes watertight; all 7 parts sliced in Bambu Studio; G-code checked by script (49.3 h, 1,523 g PETG).
Hand calculations for current, voltage drop, fuse coordination and worst-case heating (no simulation).

cost_model.intro: Per-unit cost of goods for one complete pack, without the charger, at four production volumes. Tier 1 is what the prototype costs as bought on 2026-11-15, including pack sizes (100-piece screw packs, whole sheets and spools), and values the owner's 25 hours of bench work at an assumed 35 USD per hour. The higher tiers are estimates built line by line; each line says what it rests on. A supplier quote replaces an estimate as soon as one exists.

capital_note: Stages are sequential here; S3 tooling can overlap S2 once the design is frozen. Moving to 10,000 units a year needs steel tooling and automated welding, roughly a further 0.3 to 0.6 million USD plus working capital, not included above.

ip.note: No original battery, firmware or board was opened or copied. Envelope and voltage come from published specifications.

Implemented from a description of the wire format published under the MIT licence by a third party; no code from that project is included. Interoperability with the owner's own vehicle is the purpose. Get advice on interoperability law in each target market before selling.
Brand and model names are used only to say what the pack fits. The product carries no third-party branding.
Not searched. A freedom-to-operate search is budgeted in S2.
Candidates for protection: the gateway approach (making a standard BMS speak a vehicle's battery protocol) and the holder and housing design. Novelty not assessed.

assumptions.text: Labour rates: $35/h (owner and small US shop), $15/h and $12/h fully burdened at contract manufacturers.
Charger is a separate accessory and not in the cost of goods.
The bike in the brief is a 60 V TS; a 48 V variant would use 13S and change cell count and cost.
Volume tiers are units per production run; tooling and certification are paid once and shown separately.
No shipping, import duty to the end market, distribution margin, warranty reserve or tax in the cost of goods.
